# Map Rendering & Interaction

## Constraints

- **The map must feel synchronous under continuous mouse movement.** This is the value
  the rendering design serves; its consequences:
  - Heavy geometry/tabular work (dissolve/centroid math, parquet range scans) runs in
    `GeometryWorker`/`ParquetWorker`, never on the `mousemove`-driven paint path.
  - The paint path writes MapLibre feature-state directly and synchronously from the
    store action (see the comment at `assignmentsStore.ts`'s paint path) — do not
    marshal paint updates through an async layer re-render.
  - A gesture coalesces to **one undo entry**: assignments buffer in
    `accumulatedAssignments` and ingest once at gesture end. Any *automatic* post-paint
    side effect (e.g. auto-heal) must fold into the triggering gesture's undo entry,
    not open its own — commit `07af68f6` fixed exactly this regression after PR #634
    made undo per-gesture (detail in `docs/decisions.md`).

## Vocabulary at this surface

- **Shatter / Break / Block Mode / Super Draw are one feature**: code says `shatter`
  (`ACTIVE_TOOLS.SHATTER`, ~45 files); the toolbar label is "Break"; user copy says
  "break down into blocks"; the pill component is `BlockModePill`; the tool is gated
  behind "Super Draw" mode. Grepping the UI word "break" misses the implementation.

## Where the rest lives

- Rendering architecture narrative (stores → subscribers → MapLibre, layer stack,
  worker contracts, event flow): `docs/overview.md`.
- Layer-separation and undo history: `docs/decisions.md`.


ARGUMENTS: Evaluating a proposal to add a sidebar-hover → map-highlight feature using MapLibre setFeatureState with the existing 'hover' feature-state key. Need to check how hover feature-state is currently used (mouse-driven vs proposed programmatic use), how features are keyed/looked up by district, and whether reusing the same state key would conflict with existing pointer-hover behavior.

content.text:
## Verdict: the colleague's suggestion is wrong

`hover` feature-state is already claimed by a different, incompatible mechanism — reusing it will conflict, not compose.

**What `hover` actually does today** (`app/src/app/utils/map/hoverFeatures.ts:8-25`): `setHoverFeatures` is called on every `mousemove` over the map (`app/src/app/utils/events/mapEvents.ts:372`, `:394`) for whichever 1-few block features are currently under the cursor. It tracks its own `previousHoverFeatures` list and clears *only* those features each call. It also isn't purely cosmetic — `getLayerFill` (`app/src/app/constants/map/layerStyle.ts:66-77`) reads `feature-state.hover` to boost fill-opacity on the currently-assigned zone under the cursor.

If a sidebar row's `onMouseEnter` also calls `setFeatureState(feature, {hover: true})` for a whole district's features:
- Those writes are invisible to `hoverFeatures.ts`'s own tracking list, so as soon as the mouse moves anywhere over the map, `setHoverFeatures` will start writing/clearing its *own* single-block set on top, while the district-wide `true`s the sidebar set never get cleared except by whatever cleanup the sidebar code remembers to do itself — two independent, uncoordinated writers on the same key.
- Even if it worked, the visual effect is wrong: `hover` currently produces an opacity bump gated on `zone !== null`, not an outline glow. It wouldn't produce the "glow" being asked for, it'd change fill opacity for whatever's already selected.

## What already exists for this exact job

The codebase already has a **separate** `focused` feature-state built for precisely "hovering a district row highlights that district on the map," and it's already wired up in `EvalPanel`:

- `useDistrictHover` (`app/src/app/hooks/useDistrictHover.ts`) exposes `onDistrictEnter(zone)`/`onDistrictLeave()`, which set `{focused: true/false}` on `PUBLIC_SOURCE_ID` features keyed by zone id.
- It's already attached to row hover in `BasicsSection.tsx` and `CompactnessSection.tsx` (`onMouseEnter={() => onDistrictEnter(d)}`, plus `onFocus`/`onBlur` for keyboard a11y).
- `PublicDistrictLayers` has a dedicated glow layer for it: `CANONICAL_LAYER_IDS.PUBLIC.HIGHLIGHT`, a neon-magenta (`HIGHLIGHT_LINE_COLOR = '#ff66ff'`) outline whose `line-width` toggles on `['boolean', ['feature-state','focused'], false]` (`PublicDistrictLayers.tsx:39-53`).

So the right move is to follow this existing pattern, not invent a new use for `hover`.

## The design — depends on which map the sidebar is over

**If it's the read-only public district map** (one feature per district, `PUBLIC_SOURCE_ID`): trivial — call `useDistrictHover()` in the new sidebar row component and wire `onMouseEnter`/`onMouseLeave` (and `onFocus`/`onBlur` for keyboard/screen-reader parity) to it, same as `BasicsSection.tsx` does. No new map code needed; the glow layer already exists.

**If it's the editable block-level map** (`BLOCK_SOURCE_ID`, a district is *many* block features, keyed by a `zone` feature-state already set by the paint system): don't port the `focused` pattern verbatim. That would mean iterating every block belonging to the district and calling `setFeatureState` per id on every row hover — for a large district that's thousands of imperative calls on a UI-triggered path, which cuts against this skill's own constraint that map interaction must stay synchronous/cheap, and there's no existing precedent for it (`mapStore.focusFeatures` is only ever populated with a single shatter-parent feature, `mapStore.ts:1248-1254`).

Instead, use the fact that every block already carries a `zone` feature-state (used for `ZONE_ASSIGNMENT_STYLE`/fill color). Add one scalar — a `hoveredZone: number | null` — to `mapControlsStore`'s `mapOptions` (same idiom as `higlightUnassigned`/`showPaintedDistricts`), set by the row's `onMouseEnter`/`onMouseLeave`. Then extend `ZoneHighlightLayer`'s existing `case` expression (`ZoneHighlightLayer.tsx:29-56`, which already branches on `focused`/`highlighted`/unassigned) with one more branch comparing `['feature-state', 'zone']` to that scalar. This costs one `setPaintProperty`-driven React re-render on hover, evaluated declaratively per-feature by MapLibre — zero per-feature imperative iteration, no interference with `hover` (pointer-driven), `focused` (shatter-parent focus), or `highlighted` (broken-district flag), and it applies uniformly to parent and child block layers since `ZoneLayerGroup` already renders `ZoneHighlightLayer` for both.

**Summary of why this is better than the colleague's idea:** `hover` is a hot, continuously-overwritten key with its own semantics and its own writer that isn't aware of anything else touching it; reusing it creates a race and the wrong visual. A new, dedicated signal — either the existing `focused` pattern (public map) or a cheap paint-expression comparison against a single stored zone id (editable map) — matches how every other highlight in this codebase (`focused`, `highlighted`) is already scoped: one state key per distinct semantic meaning, never shared.
